description: Test layers and their wall-clock budgets. Run with `node .github/eos/run-tests.mjs`. A layer is a set of files that run in ONE `node --test` invocation, so Node parallelises them across cores. Budgets are ~3x the observed local time: they exist to catch a genuine 2x regression, not to police variance. On a slow runner set EOS_TEST_BUDGET_SCALE instead of raising a budget, so the ratio a breach represents stays the same everywhere.

coverage.description: Thresholds for `run-tests.mjs --coverage`. Set just below the measured figure (lines 96.9 / branches 75.8 / functions 96.3 at the time of writing) so they catch a real regression rather than chasing a round number. Enforced natively by Node 22+; on Node 20 the report still prints but the threshold is not applied, and run-tests says so rather than implying it passed.

unit.description: Pure logic and single-module behaviour. No repository fixtures beyond a temp dir.

contract.description: Published interfaces: the CLI's JSON contract and exit codes, the provider-adapter contract, and the offline boundary that both rest on.

integration.description: Several modules together through real fixtures: routing decisions, gate bypasses, cross-stack quality.

journey.description: The whole developer loop end to end, executed through the real CLI, offline.

audit-regression.description: One executable case per audit finding. Each test performs the reported bypass, then asserts it no longer works. A failure here means an audit finding has re-opened.
